MATERIALS-PASS HIGHLIGHT. The check caught that led_amber was DECLARED in the spec but NEVER instantiated — every per-port lens was wired to green, so the model could not reach a state its own contract declares (and the amber evidence is the manual's state table, not a guess). Builder split the per-port row into 8 green (link) + 2 amber (disabled/fault) — visible in the ?leds=on capture as a green row with two amber lenses — and the 6-LED system column shows its amber/green mix. Illustrative, not a measurement (does not claim which ports are disabled on any real unit — same discipline as the PDU display), and asserted at exactly 2 so amber cannot silently fall out of the render again.

mechanical.notes: Console clean (0/0) across default, leds, port-detail, rear. 13/13 spec materials map 1:1 to a live material (color/metalness/roughness), zero contract drift (builder-verified headless). Budget 42/150 draws, 1744/200000 tris. Zero coincident planes — and the z-fight guard was refined twice this pass with a re-verified negative control: (1) it compared InstancedMesh object bboxes (the hull of all instances), so two interleaved instanced parts looked co-planar when their individual lenses never touch — now expands each instanced object to PER-INSTANCE boxes (occupancy, not hulls); (2) it flagged same-material grid walls that cross by construction — now skips same-material pairs, since z-fighting is only visible between surfaces that differ in appearance. Both fixes narrow the guard without softening it (pushing the port block flush still reproduces the two-DIFFERENT-material coincidence it exists to catch).
